correctness.rationale: The internal change vectors are exactly q constant types and q(q-1)^2 distinct proper triples; endpoints add <=2. Equality forces all proper triples and an equal-state visit for every symbol. Since ends are unequal states, each equal state requires >=2 incident transitions, giving n>=q(q-1)^2+2q+2. The constructed directed graph has all proper edges and two equal-state edges per symbol, balanced except start (0,1) and end (0,2); the Euler-trail criterion supplies a saturation word at the exact threshold. Appending letters preserves saturation. For the random limit the endpoint event has the stated probability and failure of internal triple coverage decays exponentially via independent blocks. The packaged Python and C++ direct checks passed; finite runs are corroboration and not infinite proof.

value.rationale: The object is the naturally measured ordered dinucleotide frequency histogram under one source-symbol loss, relevant to DNA k-mer storage/read statistics. The theorem gives a sharp all-alphabet bound on the number of distinguishable received profiles, an exact and nontrivial smallest word length realizing every possible local change type (via an Euler trail), and limiting prevalence. For DNA size q=4 the new capacity is 42 at length 46 with asymptotic saturation fraction 33/64, which is not a routine restatement of the binary six-profile result.
